paragraphs: Rav Amram the pious, Kiddushin 81a. Captive women were brought to Nehardea and housed above him. He ordered the ladder removed. As one passed, light fell; he lifted alone a ladder ten could not lift and began climbing. Halfway he shouted, 'Fire in Amram's house!' Rabbis came, saying he shamed them. Better shame here than in the world to come, he answered. He adjured his impulse to leave, and it emerged like a fiery pillar (see there). Gilgulei Neshamot, Shin 7, says Shekhem ben Ḥamor underwent mystical rectification in Rav Amram the Pious for his intercourse with Dinah daughter of Yaakov: 'Yaakov's house shall be fire'; now he escaped transgression. End of quotation. Rav Huna bar Minyomi bought tekhelet from his household. His mother left a bundle of deeds; his brothers came before Rav Naḥman, Bava Batra 151a. Yalta, Rav Naḥman's wife, treated him, beginning of HaNizzakin—not there, but Mi SheAḥazo 67b. He came before R. Ḥiyya bar Ashi, Sukkah 11a. Bava Metzia 20b: Rabbah calls him terda; see unqualified Rav Amram above. He apparently understood that figure as Rav Amram the pious. Avodah Zarah 39a: Heilprin infers that he died before Rav Yosef.
